Classification guard: the authored edge asserts association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true, mechanismCategory BIOMECHANICAL_ALTERATION). The located evidence is a surgical series of collapsed-disease wrists and a stage-dependent treatment review: individual claims require lunate imaging with staging, separate imaging of the radioscaphoid and midcarpal joints, operative history, chronology, and exclusion of the competing causes listed on the edge. The arthritis measurements come from wrists that underwent scaphocapitate arthrodesis, so the edge must not be read as unoperated natural history.

Constitutive identity guard: no kienbock-s-disease-to-avascular-necrosis edge is authored - Kienbock's disease IS osteonecrosis (lunatomalacia) of the lunate, so the generic avascular-necrosis identity is the umbrella category rather than a downstream consequence of this identity. The authored window follows the freiberg-s-infraction, gamekeeper-s-thumb, flatfoot, and generic avascular-necrosis precedents at association-only strength with BIOMECHANICAL_ALTERATION mechanism.

Duplicate-scope and boundary guards: the osteoarthritis identity already receives ten windows including the generic femoral-head avascular-necrosis window, so the target is not pre-empted; no unexplained-chronic-pain edge is authored because Kienbock pain is lesion-explained and that identity is reserved for unexplained presentations; no loss-of-use-of-extremities edge is authored because that identity is a rating-framework container for loss of use of a limb and no condition-specific Kienbock evidence of extremity loss was located; no muscle-atrophy, carpal-tunnel-syndrome, or wrist-disarticulation edge is authored (zero-record and distinct-entity guards).
governanceNotes: D1 batch 50 (2026-09-24): one bounded association edge authored - Kienbock's disease to osteoarthritis (rank 1) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true; mechanismCategory BIOMECHANICAL_ALTERATION. The proposition rests on the Luegmair and Saffar 2014 consecutive series of scaphocapitate arthrodesis for late-stage Kienbock disease, which reports functional ranges of motion and good grip strengths with substantial pain reduction (mean QuickDASH 27, range 9.1-56.3), radiographic union in nine patients with maintained carpal height and a corrected radioscaphoid angle, and - the degeneration anchor - that radiographic signs of radioscaphoid arthritis were often observed in patients with follow-up greater than 10 years; it rests also on the Kalb 2018 review of lunate necrosis treatment, which sets out a stage-dependent algorithm in which limited lunate affection is managed by immobilization or restoration, progressive collapse of a non-reconstructable lunate bone shifts treatment to mobility-preserving procedures using the still-functional articulations of the wrist, and once all functional articulations are lost only classical salvage procedures remain feasible. The lunate collapse-to-articular-loss sequence is thus documented at review level and its late arthritic consequence at series level.

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) post-surgical kinematics - the radioscaphoid arthritis was measured after scaphocapitate arthrodesis, which itself alters carpal loading, so the finding cannot be attributed purely to the natural history of the lunate lesion and the edge is framed accordingly; (ii) cross-sectional end-stage series - the wrists are grouped at end stage and the salvage literature describes procedures for a degenerating wrist, so no cohort quantifies the incidence of arthritis after an unoperated lunate osteonecrosis; (iii) stage-dependent arrest - the algorithm explicitly provides immobilization and joint-preserving options for limited disease, implying that early stages can arrest or stabilise without collapse; (iv) mixed salvage cohorts - the proximal row carpectomy and midcarpal fusion literature groups Kienbock disease with scapholunate advanced collapse and scaphoid non-union advanced collapse, which independently cause degenerative wrist change.

Negative screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) no avascular-necrosis edge - constitutive identity guard (Kienbock's disease is lunate osteonecrosis); (ii) no unexplained-chronic-pain edge - Kienbock pain is lesion-explained and the identity's boundary is unexplained presentations (identity-boundary guard); (iii) no loss-of-use-of-extremities edge - rating-framework container without condition-specific evidence of extremity loss; (iv) no muscle-atrophy or carpal-tunnel-syndrome edge - no condition-specific data located and the compression syndrome is a distinct entity (zero-record and wrong-target guards); (v) no wrist-disarticulation or hand-amputation edge - those are separate catalog identities rather than downstream consequences (wrong-target guard); (vi) duplicate-scope note: the osteoarthritis identity's existing ten windows are not pre-empted; this adds the first site-specific lunate-collapse window alongside the generic avascular-necrosis window, following the Freiberg precedent.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The Luegmair and Saffar 2014 series of scaphocapitate arthrodesis for late-stage Kienbock disease reports functional ranges of motion and good grip strengths with substantial pain reduction and a mean QuickDASH of 27 (range 9.1-56.3), radiographic union in nine patients with maintained carpal height and a corrected radioscaphoid angle, and documents that radiographic signs of radioscaphoid arthritis were often observed in patients with follow-up greater than 10 years; the Kalb 2018 review of lunate necrosis treatment sets out a stage-dependent algorithm in which limited lunate affection is managed by immobilization or restoration, progressive collapse of a non-reconstructable lunate bone shifts treatment to mobility-preserving procedures using the still-functional articulations of the wrist, and once all functional articulations are lost only classical salvage procedures are feasible; the literature documents late-stage Kienbock disease as a collapsed-lunate, degenerating-wrist pathology managed at end stage without establishing that every individual's radiocarpal or midcarpal osteoarthritis followed the lunate necrosis.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The mapping does not assert that Kienbock's disease caused an individual's wrist osteoarthritis: no natural-history cohort quantifies the incidence of radiocarpal or midcarpal arthritis after an unoperated lunate osteonecrosis, early-stage disease carries joint-preserving and immobilization options and may arrest, the located arthritis measurements come from wrists that underwent scaphocapitate arthrodesis - a procedure that itself alters carpal kinematics and loads the radioscaphoid joint - and the salvage series group Kienbock disease with scapholunate advanced collapse and scaphoid non-union advanced collapse, which independently produce degenerative wrist change; primary wrist osteoarthritis, post-traumatic arthritis after distal radius or scaphoid fracture, inflammatory arthropathy, and ulnar-impaction pathology independently produce the same degeneration.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized collapse-incongruity pathway: lunate osteonecrosis compromises subchondral bone and the articular surface, and as the bone progresses through fragmentation, collapse, and flattening the radiolunate and midcarpal contact geometry is lost, redistributing load onto the radioscaphoid and midcarpal articulations - the same collapse-to-degeneration logic the femoral-head avascular-necrosis and Freiberg infraction literature carries at their sites - so cartilage wear and arthritic change develop over years, the radiographic radioscaphoid arthritis appearing predominantly beyond ten years of follow-up; the pathway remains a hypothesis about an individual's course because early-stage disease can arrest and the located arthritis data come from surgically realigned wrists.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Late-stage Kienbock disease is documented as a collapsed-lunate condition treated with mobility-preserving or salvage procedures and long-term radiographic radioscaphoid arthritis is reported in operated wrists, but individual determination requires imaging of the lunate and of the involved joints with staging, documentation of prior trauma or inflammatory disease and of any wrist surgery, chronology, and review by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Serial radiographs, computed tomography, or magnetic resonance imaging documenting the lunate lesion with its stage (including whether collapse has occurred), the radioscaphoid and midcarpal joint spaces, and any cyst formation, sclerosis, or osteophyte at those joints; documentation of the initial presentation and the chronology of pain, weakness, and motion loss relative to any radiographic degeneration; hand-surgery or orthopaedic operative records where applicable (procedure, date, and whether any wrist fusion or realignment was performed, since surgery itself alters carpal loading); grip strength, wrist range of motion, and validated wrist outcome scores; workup excluding prior distal radius, scaphoid, or carpal trauma, ulnar-impaction or negative-ulnar-variance anatomy, inflammatory or crystal arthropathy, and primary wrist osteoarthritis; hand-surgery or orthopaedic assessment of whether the lunate necrosis and any collapse materially contributed to the documented degeneration
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Primary (idiopathic) wrist osteoarthritis unrelated to the lunate
Post-traumatic radiocarpal or midcarpal arthritis after distal radius, scaphoid, or perilunate injury
Scapholunate advanced collapse or scaphoid non-union advanced collapse
Inflammatory or crystal arthropathy (rheumatoid arthritis, gout, calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease)
Carpal collapse itself rather than joint degeneration (constitutive overlap with the lunate lesion)
Ulnar-impaction syndrome or other ulnar-sided wrist pathology

evidenceGaps: Serial radiographs, computed tomography, or magnetic resonance imaging documenting the lunate lesion with its stage (including whether collapse has occurred), the radioscaphoid and midcarpal joint spaces, and any cyst formation, sclerosis, or osteophyte at those joints; documentation of the initial presentation and the chronology of pain, weakness, and motion loss relative to any radiographic degeneration; hand-surgery or orthopaedic operative records where applicable (procedure, date, and whether any wrist fusion or realignment was performed, since surgery itself alters carpal loading); grip strength, wrist range of motion, and validated wrist outcome scores; workup excluding prior distal radius, scaphoid, or carpal trauma, ulnar-impaction or negative-ulnar-variance anatomy, inflammatory or crystal arthropathy, and primary wrist osteoarthritis; hand-surgery or orthopaedic assessment of whether the lunate necrosis and any collapse materially contributed to the documented degeneration
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: a scaphocapitate-arthrodesis series for late-stage Kienbock disease reports radiographic radioscaphoid arthritis often at follow-up beyond ten years, and a treatment review documents stage-dependent progression from limited lunate affection through progressive collapse to loss of all functional wrist articulations. Because the located arthritis data arise in surgically realigned wrists and no natural-history cohort quantifies degeneration after unoperated lunate necrosis, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only, consistent with the avascular-necrosis, Freiberg's infraction, flatfoot, and gamekeeper's-thumb windows already carried by the osteoarthritis identity.
